what: Visa runs the world's largest card-payment network. It does not lend money or issue cards itself; banks issue Visa cards and Visa earns a small fee on every transaction it processes.
customers: Banks and card issuers, merchants that accept cards, and the billions of cardholders who use them.
money: fees based on the payment volume on Visa cards
fees for authorizing, clearing and settling each transaction
higher fees on cross-border and currency-conversion payments
fraud tools, data, consulting and account-to-account payments
moat: A two-sided network: merchants accept Visa because billions carry it and people carry it because merchants accept it. Very high margins and little capital needed.
risks: Regulation of card fees in the US and Europe
Instant bank payments and digital wallets bypassing card networks
opportunities: Operating margin of 61% and return on invested capital of 40%
Revenue grew about 15% last year and about 12% a year over three years
Cash displacement by cards continues worldwide, especially outside the United States
watch: Cross-border volume growth and payment volume by region.
